observation_summary: The static initializer for the primitiveValues map in org.mockito.internal.util.Primitives contains an incorrect entry: primitiveValues.put(double.class, 0);. This assigns an Integer (0) to a map expected to return a Double for double.class, leading to ClassCastException and assertion failures in tests.
hypothesis: The class org.mockito.internal.util.Primitives incorrectly initializes the default value for double.class as an Integer (0) instead of a Double (0.0D), causing type mismatch errors when the framework attempts to return this default value.
prediction: Changing the initialization of double.class in primitiveValues to 0D will resolve the ClassCastException and the assertion failures.
experiment_rationale: The source code inspection confirmed that the entry for double.class in the primitiveValues map was initialized with an integer literal 0, which is incorrect for a double type.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic initialization error where the wrong value type was assigned to a map entry. This fits the ODC definition of Assignment/Initialization perfectly.
evidence_used: failing test stack traces showing ClassCastException (Integer to Double)

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is a simple correction of an initialized value, not a change in the logic or procedure of the method.
